title: presubmit-plumbing-refactor-add-staged-release-timelock
author: Priya Sengupta
description:
Motivation: Our presubmit plumbing had accumulated special-cased hooks and brittle release triggers that made small repo hygiene and dependency updates painful. This PR refactors the presubmit entrypoints, extracts a small 'dep freshness prober', and introduces a staged release timelock to prevent accidental fast-forward releases during release-day churn.

What this changes: 1) Centralize presubmit entrypoint: move CI bootstrap logic from multiple scripts into ci/presubmit/bootstrap.ts with typed inputs and clearer feature flags (fastpath, staged). 2) Introduce dep-freshness-prober: a lightweight Go binary (ci/tools/dep_prober) that samples package manifests and signals a minor/patch update recommendation; runs as a non-blocking presubmit step and annotates PRs with suggested upgrades. 3) Staged release timelock: add a release window gate that prevents merges to release/* branches during configured blackout windows unless explicit release-manager override label is present. 4) Split lint/test pipelines: lint still runs early-fast in a slim node image; full typecheck and integration tests are staged into a later lane to improve feedback latency for small changes. 5) Repo hygiene: normalize workspace node versions, remove duplicate precommit hooks, and add a lightweight migration doc.

Checklist: - [x] preserve backwards compatibility for existing presubmit flags - [x] CI green on main matrix (linux/mac) - [x] migration guide in docs/ci/README.md - [x] smoke-tested a release branch with timelock disabled via override label - [x] linear tickets linked: ENG-3247, ENG-3301

Migration notes: - Existing automation that invoked legacy ./ci/run-presubmit.sh should switch to node ./ci/presubmit/bootstrap.ts or the thin wrapper in scripts/run-presubmit for a transitional period. - Release automation must respect the new TIMED_RELEASE_BLACKOUT env var; operators can temporarily opt-out with label release/force-merge. - Dep prober annotations are non-blocking by default; to make them gating we will follow-up with ENG-3301.

Rollback plan: revert the presubmit bootstrap file and re-enable legacy script symlinks; timelock is controlled by a single configmap in .github/release-timelock.yaml so disabling is fast.

Related: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-3247/presubmit-plumbing-refactor and https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-3301/dep-prober-integration

review_comments: Ethan Morales: Nice consolidation — can we avoid a cold-start penalty for small PRs? Suggest adding a cached warm layer to Dockerfile.slim.
Priya Sengupta: Good point, added a small cache-warm step and reduced the base image layers; see Dockerfile.slim change.
Linnea Berg: The timelock concept is sound, but we need a clear audit log for overrides. Please add event logging when release/force-merge is used.
Priya Sengupta: Added simple webhook-emission on override and a README section that documents audit expectations.
Martin Koh: Dep prober output looks useful. Suggest we limit file-system IO on large monorepos — can the prober sample rather than walk everything?
Priya Sengupta: Implemented sampling on top-level manifests and a fast-path for monorepo roots with manifest index; added unit tests.

release_notes: Refactor presubmit plumbing: centralizes bootstrap, adds non-blocking dependency freshness prober, and adds a staged release timelock to prevent accidental merges during blackout windows. Improves small-PR feedback latency by splitting lint fastpath and staged integration lanes.
additional_context: This PR intentionally keeps dep_prober non-gating for now to avoid blocking the release cadence; after gathering signals we'll roll in a gating policy. We also standardized the node toolchain to 20.x across workspaces to reduce CI image churn.
attention_requests: Owners for release automation (Martin Koh) and infra (Ethan Morales) asked to confirm rollout schedule; ops will enable timelock in production after a one-week soak on staging.
